title.description: One-line preview of the first filtered human prompt, cut to 72 characters through parser 0.17.0 or 128 characters from parser 0.17.1. From parser 0.19.0 the <timestamp> line and <user_query> tags Cursor wraps a prompt in are not part of it. Omitted when no prompt text was available.

name.description: From parser 0.17.0: the title the harness gave the session, collapsed to one line and cut to 72 characters through parser 0.17.0 or 128 characters from parser 0.17.1, like title: Claude Code's custom title (the last one, when the session was renamed) or a Cursor chat's name; from parser 0.18.0 a Claude Code subagent's name is the description its parent gave the task. Absent when the session has none.

branch.description: From parser 0.17.0: the last git branch the transcript recorded. Absent when none was recorded, it is HEAD (a detached checkout), or it is not a valid branch name.

pull_requests.description: From parser 0.17.0: the pull requests the session was linked to (Claude Code's pr-link records), in the order first linked, each once, at most 20. Absent when there are none.

project_name.description: Basename of the session's project root at publish time, for list without local config.

repo_key.description: From parser 0.16.0: identifies the git repository the session ran in, independent of where it is checked out. 'repo-' plus 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the normalized origin remote URL (host/owner/repo, credentials, scheme, port and .git removed); only this hash is stored, never the URL. Absent when the project had no origin remote a second machine could reach, or the project was gone when the metadata was derived.

git_head.description: The commit the session's working directory had checked out, as the session's own hooks recorded it by running git there (a linked worktree's own HEAD; a submodule's when the session ran inside one). 'start' is HEAD, with whether the working tree was dirty, when the hook that registered the session ran; 'last' is HEAD at the most recent stop hook that could read it. Either is absent when no hook could tell (git not installed, not a repository, a branch with no commits, git slower than the hook's budget) 'start' is also absent on sessions registered before this field or imported by backfill; a later live stop can record 'last'. Subagents have neither. Neither is ever inferred afterwards. Only commit names, a boolean, and times are recorded: never a branch, remote, path, or file name. The commit may exist only on the capturing machine.

last.description: Replaced only when a stop hook finds HEAD at a different commit, so observed_at is the first stop that saw this commit. Carries no dirty flag.

ended_at.description: From parser 0.13.0: the latest timestamp any retained record of the session carries (the maximum, since records may be out of order), never earlier than started_at. Absent when no record carries a timestamp (a Cursor transcript) or the source could not be parsed.

status.description: How far the parser vouches for this metadata. 'complete': the adapter has shown it understands every retained record, and list --complete requires it. 'partial' (the default): the metadata was derived, but the parser does not claim to understand every record, so counts and models may be incomplete. 'failed': the filtered source could not be parsed; only identity, the source reference, and hook-derived lifecycle are filled in, and a later parser version may retry.

counts.description: Every count is optional: an absent count is unknown, never zero. From parser 0.6.0 'turns' counts human prompts (a user record with text or any non-tool-result content), 'messages' counts those prompts plus assistant records, and 'tool_results' counts observed tool results. From parser 0.7.0 a harness-written user record (isMeta, local-command or shell output, or a slash command no assistant answered) is not a prompt, 'messages' counts distinct assistant message ids (a record without an id counts on its own), and 'user_shell_commands' counts shell commands the person ran directly (Claude Code '!' commands). From parser 0.8.0 a Claude Code compaction summary (a user record marked isCompactSummary) is neither a prompt nor a message, and 'compactions' counts how many times the session was compacted (/compact or auto-compaction), from compact_boundary records or, when none was retained, from compaction summaries; it is present only for Claude Code sessions captured with filter 5 or later. From parser 0.9.0 a harness-written notification (origin.kind 'task-notification') is not a prompt. From parser 0.10.0 Claude Code's '[Request interrupted by user…]' marker is not a prompt, 'tool_calls' no longer counts tool-call shapes found inside another call's arguments, a Cursor text transcript's role sections start only at a header in column 0, and a message Claude Code synthesized itself (model '<synthetic>') names no model and adds no tokens. From parser 0.11.0 a Cursor text transcript's role header is lower case ('user:', not 'User:'), and when its sections are separated by blank lines a role line that does not follow one is content; token totals saturate at 2^53 instead of overflowing. The token counts are summed from whatever the harness exposed, counting only whole numbers from 0 to 2^53 (anything else in a record is ignored), and are absent when it exposed none.

files_touched.description: From parser 0.13.0: how many distinct files the session's recognized editing calls (Edit, Write, apply_patch, edit_file, and the like) named; a path under the workspace root and the same path relative to it count once. Only the count is published, never a path.

cache_write_tokens.description: Claude Code's cache_creation_input_tokens, or, from parser 0.14.0, Codex's cache_write_input_tokens.

reasoning_tokens.description: From parser 0.14.0: tokens the model spent reasoning (Claude Code's output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens, Codex's reasoning_output_tokens), summed like the other token counts. It is part of output_tokens, not in addition to it. Absent when the harness reported none.

tool_errors.description: From parser 0.14.0: how many of tool_results the harness marked as errors (is_error true). Known wherever tool_results is, for Claude Code and Cursor. Absent for Codex, which writes no such flag: its count is unknown, not zero.

commits.description: From parser 0.15.0: commits the session's tool calls confirmed (git commit output naming the new commit, or a GitHub MCP tool that committed on the server). Present wherever tool_calls is; uncapped, unlike git_activity.

pushes.description: From parser 0.15.0: refs a git push the session ran reported updating or creating. Rejected, up-to-date, and dry-run pushes are not counted.

prs_created.description: From parser 0.15.0: pull requests the session created (gh pr create printing the new pull request's URL, or a GitHub MCP create_pull_request result).

prs_merged.description: From parser 0.15.0: pull requests the session merged (gh pr merge's confirmation, or a GitHub MCP merge_pull_request result reporting the merge). Enabling auto-merge is not a merge.

model_tokens.description: From parser 0.14.0: the session's token counts split by model, sorted by model id. Each entry uses the field meanings of counts. A record whose usage names no model is counted under the model 'unknown'. A model id longer than 128 characters is cut to that, and at most 32 entries are kept: beyond that, the models with the fewest tokens are added together under the model 'other', so the sums hold. For Claude Code the model is the one named on the response message; for Codex, the model of the latest turn_context before the token record, so a model switched mid-session splits the counts at the switch. Streamed duplicates of one Claude Code message count once, as in counts. Below 2^53 tokens each token field of counts is the sum of that field over model_tokens, and both are absent when the harness exposed no token accounting (Cursor's unmetered zeros are not accounting).

mcp_calls.description: From parser 0.14.0: the session's MCP tool calls counted by server (the server in an mcp__<server>__<tool> tool name), by count descending and then name ascending, at most 50. Absent when no such call was observed or the counts are unknown. Codex's MCP calls do not name their server in what is retained, so they are not counted.

git_activity.description: From parser 0.15.0: the commits, pushes, and pull requests created or merged that the session's own tool calls confirmed, in transcript order, at most 100 (counts.commits, pushes, prs_created, and prs_merged stay exact). An event is recorded only when the call's result was linked, is not an error, and its output shows the effect; a failed, rejected, or dry-run attempt is not an event. Shell commands (git, gh) and GitHub MCP tools are recognized. Only identifiers are kept: never a commit message, pull request text, or command line. Absent when no such event was observed or the counts are unknown.

tools_used.description: From parser 0.13.0: the session's most-called tools, by call count descending and then name ascending, at most 10. Names are the harness's own (MCP tools included, e.g. mcp__server__tool), credential-redacted, on one line, and at most 128 characters. Absent when no named tool call was observed or the counts are unknown; counts.tool_calls tells the two apart.

native_child.description: Native child ownership, independent of parent link availability.

origin.description: Admission provenance. From parser 0.20.0 discovery has no imported_at and preserves a discovered_without_hook_evidence gap; later hooks do not establish earlier lifecycle coverage.

replay.description: Present only for a session a replay tool ran: the environment variable AGENT_ARCHIVE_REPLAY was set (non-empty) in the hook that registered it. list, stats, and handoff leave such sessions out unless asked (list --replays include|only). Fixed at registration, so a continuation never adds or removes it; a subagent carries its parent's. An object even without a run_id, so a reader tests for the key, not the value.

run_id.description: The variable's value when it is an identifier: 1 to 128 ASCII letters, digits, '.', '_', ':' or '-', starting with a letter or digit. Absent when the value was anything else, which is never recorded.

imported_at.description: When this machine imported the session. Present only with origin 'import'.

started_at_source.description: Where started_at came from: 'hook' when a hook observed the start, 'transcript' the earliest native record, 'file_created' the transcript file's birth time (Cursor transcripts, whose records have no timestamps), and 'cursor_composer' the chat's creation time in Cursor's database (a chat imported from it). Present for import and discovery origins.

previous_generation_id.description: Previous archive generation, independent of parent_session_id subagent lineage.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the skill's SKILL.md with its credentials redacted (from filter 12; earlier filters hashed the original bytes). A file with nothing to redact hashes to its own SHA-256.

attributes.description: OpenTelemetry gen_ai.* attributes (see semantic_conventions) and agent_archive.* local extensions.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the skill's SKILL.md with its credentials redacted (from filter 12; earlier filters hashed the original bytes). A file with nothing to redact hashes to its own SHA-256.

detail.description: Archive-authored description of the omission. Never a transcript value. From filter version 3 the single unknown_field_omitted gap carries the distinct omitted key names, sorted and capped, as 'omitted keys: a, b, c'. A subagent_transcript_never_written gap carries the fixed text 'Claude Code reported a subagent but never wrote its transcript'.

gap_code.description: An archive-authored reason. The enum lists every code this version writes (internal/archive CaptureGapCodes; dev/specs/privacy-filter.md says what each means). A reader must accept any other lowercase code, which an older or newer writer may use.

sha.description: HEAD's full object name: 40 hex digits (SHA-1) or 64 (SHA-256).

dirty.description: Whether the working tree had staged, unstaged, or untracked (not ignored) changes against sha. A submodule counts when its checked-out commit differs, not for changes inside it. Absent when unknown.

observed_at.description: The time of the hook event that saw it.

sha.description: HEAD's full object name: 40 hex digits (SHA-1) or 64 (SHA-256).

observed_at.description: The time of the hook event that saw it.

url.description: The pull request's GitHub address, https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<number>, kept only in exactly that form. Absent when the record carried none.

kind.description: What happened. A reader must accept any other lowercase kind, which a newer writer may add.

at.description: The timestamp of the record carrying the confirming result. Absent when the harness wrote none.

source.description: Which recognizer confirmed the event: a shell command's output, or an MCP tool's result.

sha.description: A commit event's new commit (git commit prints it abbreviated), a push's new tip (absent for a new branch, whose report names none), or a merge's commit when the result reported one.

branch.description: The branch committed to or pushed, or a pull request's head branch when known.

repository.description: owner/repo, from the push remote, the pull request URL, or the MCP call's owner and repo.

pr_number.description: The pull request's number; pull request kinds only.

url.description: Rebuilt from the parsed host, repository, and branch or number (https://<host>/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<n>, or /tree/<branch> for a push), never copied from output. Absent when the host is unknown or is not a public DNS name (a local git proxy).
